themes.definition: Decision-making centered on avoiding bias and maintaining neutrality (including balancing evaluations across left/right viewpoints), even when viewpoints feel far-reaching or asymmetrical.
Moderation choices were driven primarily by whether language was vulgar/offensive (or whether profanity alone mattered), with political content explicitly treated as secondary.

themes.theme_label: Free-speech balancing with uncertainty about moderation boundaries
themes.definition: Participants justify or resist removals using free-speech principles while expressing discomfort/uncertainty about where to draw the line versus misinformation or harmful conduct.

themes.theme_label: Emotional reactivity to extremity/aggression (including rage-bait suspicion)
themes.definition: Evaluation relied on emotional response to aggression/extremity (e.g., anger/sadness/dislike) and sometimes suspected intent such as rage bait, rather than detailed pair-based comparison.

themes.theme_label: Minimal reasoning / heuristics (randomness, craziness, terse criteria)
themes.definition: Responses used very limited or single heuristics (e.g., 'it was random' or 'how crazy it was') and/or provided sparse rationales that bypass substantive pair comparison.
